commit.message:
fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser (#468)

* fix: suppress DEP0190 deprecation when auto-opening browser

Starting pi-web on Windows prints a Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning:

  (node:XXXXX) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child
  process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities,
  as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.

This is emitted by the browser auto-open call, which used
`spawn(openCmd, [url], { shell: isWindows })`. DEP0190 triggers
whenever args are passed together with `shell: true`.

Refactor the call to avoid `shell: true` entirely while preserving
the same auto-open behavior:
- Windows: invoke `cmd.exe /c start "" <url>` directly so the URL
  is passed as a structured argv (the empty title is required by the
  `start` built-in).
- macOS / Linux: spawn `open` / `xdg-open` without `shell`.

* fix: validate browser launch port

---------

Co-authored-by: Zach Chiu <zack@hku.com.tw>
Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: resolve hydration mismatch from browser extensions and responsive aria-valuemax (#463)

Two sources of hydration mismatch on initial page load:

1. Browser extensions (Grammarly, translation, password managers) mutate
   the <body> element's attributes before React hydrates. <html> already
   had suppressHydrationWarning but <body> did not.

2. The sidebar resize separator's aria-valuemax was computed via
   effectiveMaxWidth() during render, which calls getMaxWidth(). On the
   server this returns the constant maxWidth, but on the client it
   returns a viewport-dependent value, causing a mismatch for viewports
   between 641px and 799px wide. Gate the responsive computation behind
   a mounted flag so the initial render uses the constant maxWidth.

commit.message:
Strip skill XML from session auto-naming (#457)

A new session whose first message is a /skill: invocation stores the
SDK-expanded <skill> block as the message, so the no-name fallback
(firstMessage.slice(0, 50)) leaked that XML into the sidebar title and
the rename input. Collapse such blocks to the compact /skill:name args
command via the existing skillExpansionToCommand helper before slicing,
mirroring MessageView's rendering.

The rename input seeds from the same collapsed form, so an untouched
rename of a skill-invoked session stays a no-op instead of persisting
the raw XML as the session name.

commit.message:
fix: custom headers and compat for custom models (#456)

* feat: add headers and compat for custom models

Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints often need per-request headers
(such as User-Agent for gateway bot detection) and a compat flag to
fall back to the system role when the server rejects the developer
role. These previously required hand-editing models.json.

* headers editor at both provider and model level, with model-level
  values overriding the provider for that model
* supportsDeveloperRole toggle reads the effective provider-plus-model
  compat value and writes an explicit per-model override

* fix: persist model compat and header drafts

perf: skip syntax highlighting while a message is streaming (#433)

* perf: cut streamed-render CPU — skip Prism while streaming, memoize CodeBlock and toolResults map

Streaming updates re-rendered the live message on every SSE message_update,
re-tokenizing the whole growing code block with Prism each time. Render code
fences as plain monospace text while the message is streaming and highlight
once on completion.

Also memoize CodeBlock (unchanged code must not re-run tokenization when the
parent markdown re-renders) and hoist ChatWindow's toolResults Map into a
useMemo keyed on messages so its identity stays stable across streaming
updates.

* fix: stabilize Mermaid preview action

commit.message:
feat: play completion sound for tasks finishing in other workspaces (#417)

The completion tone previously lived in ChatWindow, so only the active
session could ring. Audio ownership moves up to AppShell so a task that
finishes in a non-active workspace (whose ChatWindow is not mounted) can
still notify. SessionSidebar already detects completedInBackground while
polling running sessions; it now reports those via a new onBackgroundTaskDone
callback, and AppShell plays the tone when the sound toggle is enabled.

ChatWindow now receives the audio state and controls as props instead of
owning its own AudioContext.

commit.message:
feat: restore the last-open session when switching workspaces (#416)

* feat: restore the last-open session when switching workspaces

Switching to a workspace previously landed on a blank new-session page and
the session open there last had to be re-picked by hand. Record the
selected session per workspace (resolved project root, sharing one slot
across worktrees) in localStorage, and on a cross-project cwd change
look it up against the live session list to restore it.

A deleted or drifted session clears the memory and keeps the welcome
page; a failed list fetch keeps the memory for a later retry. A token
guard drops stale async restores after a rapid switch sequence.

* fix: stabilize workspace session restoration

---------

Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows (#388)

* fix: compare git-emitted paths correctly on Windows

`git rev-parse --path-format=absolute` prints POSIX-style absolute paths
even on Windows (`D:/repo`), while `realpathSync()` and the session cwds
recorded by pi are native (`D:\repo`). `resolveProject()` compared the two
with `===`, so on Windows:

- `isTopLevel` was permanently false, which hid the worktree switcher
  entirely and left only the disabled "Open repo root" hint;
- `isWorktreeTopLevel` was therefore also always false, so linked
  worktrees never collapsed into the main repo's `projectRoot` and each
  showed up as a separate phantom project instead of being grouped;
- `listWorktrees()` returned slash-style paths that never matched
  `selectedCwd`, breaking the current-worktree highlight in the sidebar.

Route every path read out of git through `toNativePath()` and compare with
`samePath()`, which also tolerates drive-letter case since Windows paths
are case-insensitive. Branch names deliberately skip normalization so
`feature/x` does not become `feature\x`.

Both helpers live in a new `lib/paths.ts` alongside `isWindowsAbsolutePath()`,
which had been duplicated in `lib/file-access.ts` and `lib/path-security.ts`.
`isFilePathAllowed()` was a byte-for-byte copy of `isPathWithinRoots()` and
now delegates to it, leaving one implementation of the access-control check.
The allowed-roots set keeps its slash-normalized form: it is an internal Set
key that is never displayed, and containment checks re-normalize both sides
anyway, so both path forms authorize identically.

Verified on Windows against real repositories: repo roots now resolve as
top-level, subdirectories still do not, linked worktrees collapse to the
main repo, and `feature/x` keeps its slash. Adds `lib/paths.test.mjs`
covering separator style, drive-letter case and UNC paths.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: canonicalize worktree identity end to end

* test: isolate worktree sidebar regression

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: render YAML frontmatter as a metadata card in markdown preview (#391)

react-markdown has no frontmatter support, so a leading `---` block was
parsed as CommonMark instead: the opening `---` became an <hr> and the
closing `---` turned the YAML lines into a setext heading, leaking raw
metadata like `title: My Doc` into the rendered preview between two
horizontal rules (and letting remark-math mangle any $ inside it).

- Add remark-frontmatter (yaml only) to both render pipelines so the
  block parses as a `yaml` node and disappears from the rendered output.
- Add parseFrontmatter() (lib/markdown.ts) backed by js-yaml, and a
  FrontmatterCard that renders the metadata above the preview body:
  `title` as a heading, `tags`/`categories`/`keywords` as chips, remaining
  keys as a key/value table with http(s)/mailto values as links.
- Malformed YAML shows no card but is still hidden by the remark plugin;
  documents without frontmatter render exactly as before.

Verified with tsc --noEmit and eslint; the parse pipeline was also
checked with unified directly (frontmatter yields no output, and the
setext-trap / mid-document `---` cases still parse as CommonMark).

Co-authored-by: Alex Yang <agegcn@gmail.com>

commit.message:
fix: don't misparse in-hunk diff lines as file headers (#394)

parseUnifiedPatch checked every line for a "--- "/"+++ " file header,
including lines inside a hunk body. A removed line whose content starts
with "-- " (raw line "--- ...") or an added line whose content starts
with "++ " (raw line "+++ ...") was therefore misread as a new file
header: flushChanges() ran mid-hunk and a bogus extra SplitDiffFile was
started, corrupting the split-diff view. This happens for ordinary
content — Markdown/reStructuredText bullets, and especially diffs that
themselves contain diff text.

Track the remaining line counts from the @@ hunk header (defaulting an
omitted count to 1) and only look for file headers when outside a hunk
body. Inside a hunk, "--- ..."/"+++ ..." lines fall through to the normal
-/+ content handling.

Adds regression tests for header-like in-hunk content and for resuming
header detection across multiple files.

commit.message:
fix: don't treat a single tilde as strikethrough (CJK ranges) (#392)

`~` is the standard CJK notation for numeric ranges (e.g. "5~7U",
"100~200倍"). GFM strikethrough accepts a single tilde as a delimiter, so
any assistant message with two `~` in one paragraph had the tildes
dropped and an arbitrary span struck through - silently corrupting the
content (a "5~7U" range renders as "57U"). This is common in LLM output
for CJK users.

Pass singleTilde:false to remark-gfm (its supported option) so
strikethrough requires ~~double~~ tildes, leaving single-tilde ranges
literal. Applied via the shared markdown plugin config, so chat, file
preview, and the minimap all honor it.

Fixes #385

fix: keep file icons monochrome in dark theme (#412)

The base html.dark .catppuccin-file-icon rule re-applies the colorful Mocha SVG as background-image on top of the monochrome gray set by the @supports background shorthand (higher specificity), so dark mode bled the language colors back through the semi-transparent mask. Mirror the light-theme rule by adding background: var(--text-dim) in the masked html.dark branch, which clears the image wherever mask-image is supported while preserving the graceful fallback.

feat: list turn-written files under each reply and open HTML in preview (#378)

* feat: derive the files a turn wrote from its write/edit tool calls

extractTurnWrittenFiles collects the distinct files an assistant turn
wrote, keeping only write/edit tool calls whose result arrived and did not
error, resolving each path against cwd and deduping by absolute path.

The tool call is the evidence that a file was written. A path the
assistant merely mentions in its reply is not, so the reply text is never
scanned; tests cover that case explicitly.

lib/tool-names.ts holds the write/edit name predicates so this and the
chat views stay in agreement.

commit.message:
feat: browser notification when agent session ends (#356)

* feat: browser notification when agent session ends

Closes #339. Ref discussion #317.

When the tab is in the background, fires a Web Notifications API popup
on agent completion. The notification title uses the current session
name (falls back to i18n "Session complete"); the body is the i18n
"Task finished." string, so both en and zh-CN are covered.

Permission is requested lazily on the first background completion;
denied or unsupported browsers are silently skipped.

* feat: focus session from completion notifications

commit.message:
feat: collapse slash command expansion in user messages (#338)

Show a compact clickable command reference for slash-command messages
(/skill:name and prompt templates) instead of the full SDK-expanded
text. The user-supplied arguments stay fully visible; clicking the
command name toggles the expanded skill/template body.

- lib/slash-display.ts: pure helpers (command parsing, skill expansion
  reverse-matching, FIFO tracker) + 17 unit tests
- rpc-manager.ts: inject originalText on message_end for user messages
  via a new message object (never mutates SDK-shared state), always
  consume one FIFO entry per message, clear the tracker on prompt
  failures
- session-reader.ts: reverse-match skill expansions when loading
  session history
- MessageView.tsx: render command name as accent-colored toggle with
  args shown verbatim; keep image blocks in both branches; add
  aria-expanded

Storage and model input stay unchanged: session JSONL keeps the
expanded text and originalText is a display-only field.

commit.message: feat: play sound for extension dialogs

feat: group dormant skills in skills panel and slash palette (#288)

* feat: group dormant skills in skills panel and slash palette

Skills with disable-model-invocation (dormant) now get their own
visual treatment:

- Skills panel: within each scope group, dormant skills are tucked
  into a collapsed-by-default "Dormant (N)" subsection; groups
  without dormant skills render exactly as before
- Slash palette: the skill group lists active commands first and
  dormant commands last, dimmed with a small dormant badge. Skill
  dormancy is lazy-fetched from /api/skills each time the palette
  opens so toggles in the skills panel are reflected on next open;
  fetch failures silently fall back to the unannotated palette
- Skill detail toggle now notes that the change applies to new
  sessions

Display-layer only; no API or RPC behavior changes.

* fix: harden dormant skill interactions

* fix: stabilize dormant skill toggle layout

---------

Co-authored-by: Hermes Agent <hermes@nousresearch.com>
